summary: I held the optimizer/LR-schedule surface after a 5-way collision on batch-size and shape, and my family turned out to be a flat/tuned basin: Muon MATRIX_LR +50% was neutral (0.996579 vs 0.997359 at 2^19), UNEMBEDDING_LR x3 was mildly worse (+0.0016), WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5->0.8 was neutral (+0.0002), momentum target 0.95->0.98 was clearly worse (+0.0059) and 0.95->0.90 free (-0.0004). The one transferable result is the asymmetry: momentum sits at the upper edge of its basin, so re-tuning should move it down, never up. All real gains in the cell came from peers' levers, which I adopted in sequence (a4 batch 2^18 -> a1 depth 10 -> a2 dim 768 -> a0 three-way merge); my final run combined a0's depth-8/dim-768/window-256/VE-first3-last3 base with a4's 197K-token batch and my momentum 0.90 for 0.976458, statistically identical to the same merge at momentum 0.95 (dd7cd01, 0.976408), which is itself the cleanest confirmation that the momentum knob is a null. Next I would stop tuning the optimizer and spend runs on the width/throughput frontier: dim 768 won but dim 896 blew up (0.993-1.031 at forced device batch 64), so a chunked/fused cross-entropy that frees the 34GB fp32 logits tensor is the prerequisite for testing dim 896+ at device batch 96-128.
